{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MU6UAQxLMkxAwsSz15gejp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\t`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.\n9\t\n10\tFor a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.\n11\t\n12\tRaised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tDecide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:\n17\t\n18\t- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.\n19\t- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.\n20\t\n21\tWhichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.\n22\t\n23\t## Acceptance criteria\n24\t\n25\t- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts\n26\t- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited\n27\t- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing\n28\t- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum\n29\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record\n30\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API\n31\t\n32\t## Tech notes\n33\t\n34\tOut of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.\n35\t\n36\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n37\t\n38\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"81fa0875-69f4-4c72-b716-9a638a5bb0f3","uuid":"2022a5d7-8690-405b-bd74-3e1db5e0de27","timestamp":"2026-11-07T03:22:32.015Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/f9eaa477d12b/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93\nLabels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\n`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.\n\nFor a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.\n\nRaised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.\n\n## What to do\n\nDecide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:\n\n- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.\n- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.\n\nWhichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts\n- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited\n- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing\n- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum\n- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record\n- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API\n\n## Tech notes\n\nOut of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.\n\nKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n\n","numLines":38,"startLine":1,"totalLines":38}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01MU6UAQxLMkxAwsSz15gejp","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UrZcpDYDG2BPMxf6Tysr8J","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n6\t| Status | Shipped              |\n7\t\n8\t`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n9\t\n10\t## Installing hooks through config\n11\t\n12\t- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n13\t- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n14\t- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n15\t- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n16\t- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n17\t- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n18\t\n19\t## Engine startup\n20\t\n21\t- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n22\t\n23\t## Measured semantics — out of scope\n24\t\n25\tThese properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` record the measured semantics that hook features specify against. The `onError` boundary remains out of scope; issue #93 defines the aggregate usage delivered after tool rounds.\n26\t\n27\t- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n28\t- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and receives the summed provider-call usage for the entire turn, so tool rounds are included in a deployer's billing or audit total ([validated by: reports the summed usage from every provider call in a turn with two tool rounds](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L44)).\n29\t- A turn where some provider calls report no usage still counts the ones that do; a turn where no call reports usage delivers `undefined` from the hook rather than zero or NaN ([validated by: counts reported rounds while leaving a turn with no reported usage undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L67)).\n30\t- `accumulateUsage` maintains the running total: when the total is not yet set, the first round's usage becomes it ([validated by: returns the first round when accumulator is undefined](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L12)).\n31\t- Each token field — input, output, and total — is summed independently across rounds that contribute usage ([validated by: sums token fields from both values](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L17)).\n32\t- A round reporting no usage is skipped; the running total carries over unchanged ([validated by: returns the accumulator unchanged when the round reports no usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L23)).\n33\t- When no round in a turn contributes usage, the total stays `undefined`, so a turn that produced no usage data delivers nothing rather than a zero count ([validated by: returns undefined when neither argument has usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L28)).\n34\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"81fa0875-69f4-4c72-b716-9a638a5bb0f3","uuid":"c0db7211-f5e5-4490-9e5b-e65bb7708c55","timestamp":"2026-11-07T03:22:42.181Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/f9eaa477d12b/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md","content":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n\n## Measured semantics — out of scope\n\nThese properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` record the measured semantics that hook features specify against. The `onError` boundary remains out of scope; issue #93 defines the aggregate usage delivered after tool rounds.\n\n- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and receives the summed provider-call usage for the entire turn, so tool rounds are included in a deployer's billing or audit total ([validated by: reports the summed usage from every provider call in a turn with two tool rounds](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L44)).\n- A turn where some provider calls report no usage still counts the ones that do; a turn where no call reports usage delivers `undefined` from the hook rather than zero or NaN ([validated by: counts reported rounds while leaving a turn with no reported usage undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L67)).\n- `accumulateUsage` maintains the running total: when the total is not yet set, the first round's usage becomes it ([validated by: returns the first round when accumulator is undefined](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L12)).\n- Each token field — input, output, and total — is summed independently across rounds that contribute usage ([validated by: sums token fields from both values](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L17)).\n- A round reporting no usage is skipped; the running total carries over unchanged ([validated by: returns the accumulator unchanged when the round reports no usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L23)).\n- When no round in a turn contributes usage, the total stays `undefined`, so a turn that produced no usage data delivers nothing rather than a zero count ([validated by: returns undefined when neither argument has usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L28)).\n","numLines":34,"startLine":1,"totalLines":34}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01UrZcpDYDG2BPMxf6Tysr8J","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013vPPEFoHD2943zzypk2Q7q","type":"tool_result","content":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n\n## Measured semantics — out of scope\n\nThese properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` record the measured semantics that hook features specify against. The `onError` boundary remains out of scope; issue #93 defines the aggregate usage delivered after tool rounds.\n\n- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and receives the summed provider-call usage for the entire turn, so tool rounds are included in a deployer's billing or audit total ([validated by: reports the summed usage from every provider call in a turn with two tool rounds](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L44)).\n- A turn where some provider calls report no usage still counts the ones that do; a turn where no call reports usage delivers `undefined` from the hook rather than zero or NaN ([validated by: counts reported rounds while leaving a turn with no reported usage undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestratorUsage.acceptance.test.ts#L67)).\n- `accumulateUsage` maintains the running total: when the total is not yet set, the first round's usage becomes it ([validated by: returns the first round when accumulator is undefined](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L12)).\n- Each token field — input, output, and total — is summed independently across rounds that contribute usage ([validated by: sums token fields from both values](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L17)).\n- A round reporting no usage is skipped; the running total carries over unchanged ([validated by: returns the accumulator unchanged when the round reports no usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L23)).\n- When no round in a turn contributes usage, the total stays `undefined`, so a turn that produced no usage data delivers nothing rather than a zero count ([validated by: returns undefined when neither argument has usage](../../src/orchestration/orchestratorHelpers.test.ts#L28)).","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"81fa0875-69f4-4c72-b716-9a638a5bb0f3","uuid":"d1dd6d52-438b-469f-945e-a40ac94722c8","timestamp":"2026-11-07T03:24:10.620Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object.
